query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a gradient nanostructured surface layer on a conventional metal via surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) will concurrently improve strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: A conventional coarse-grained metal with a uniform microstructure.
generation.intervention: Application of SMAT (or a similar gradient heterostructuring technique) to create a nanograined surface layer with a continuous grain-size gradient into the bulk.
generation.conditions: Ambient temperature under standard mechanical loading conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: A gradient distribution of grain sizes where the surface possesses nanograins transitioning to a core of larger, more ductile grains.
generation.mechanism: The nanograined surface increases strength through grain-boundary strengthening, while the underlying coarse-grained region retains good ductility. The gradient structure promotes heterogeneous deformation and strain partitioning, allowing for both high strength and maintained plasticity.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in yield strength (direction: positive) alongside maintained or slightly enhanced ductility compared to the untreated metal, with expected improvements in strength on the order of 20–30% relative to the baseline.
generation.baseline: Untreated metal with uniform coarse grains exhibiting established mechanical properties (i.e., standard yield strength and ductility levels).
generation.boundary: The hypothesis may not hold if the gradient layer is too shallow or the treatment parameters lead to excessive brittleness. It might also be limited in metals where intrinsic material responses to severe plastic deformation lead to premature failure.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement in strength and ductility depends on the material composition, processing parameters, and depth of the gradient layer. Precise values and effects may vary with experimental conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare sets of metal samples subjected to varying durations of SMAT to generate different gradient depths. Evaluate mechanical properties through tensile testing and characterize microstructure using electron microscopy to confirm the gradient formation.
measurements: Grain size distribution across the depth (via microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with an induced gradient do not show a statistically significant increase in yield strength without a reduction in ductility compared to the untreated baseline, or if the gradient structure is not reproducible, then the hypothesis is falsified.
